text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The government has prepared a list of 40,000 defaulters of banks and DFIs who would be barred from taking part in the election if they fail to repay their dues. The list will be made public next week.

- Supporters of the Revolutionary Association of the Women of Afghanistan called on freedom-loving, democratic organisations of Pakistan and other countries to raise their voice against the disastrous situation in Afghanistan.
- Two apex trade bodies are to lobby the government against State (central) Bank of Pakistan's order to banks to halt all loan rescheduling until after the February 3 election.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Asian Development Bank proposes to extend $468 million assistance to Pakistan in 1997 against $500 million in 1996.
- The government is negotiating a structural adjustment programme with the World Bank, OECF of Japan and Asian Development Bank covering privatisation, banking reforms and safety nets.
- The caretaker government has decided in principle to privatise publicly-owned real estate units including the Utility Stores Corporation.
- The central bank has asked all financial institutions to list loans of 500,000 rupees or more on which repayments became 365 days overdue on December 1.
FINANCIAL POST
- The World Bank said lack of fiscal discipline in Pakistan's financial sector and intermediation project could put upward pressure on inflation and nominal interest rates.
- The Ministry of Finance does not intend to invite competitive bids for the planned $150 million five-year Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd convertible bonds issue.
- The caretaker government may devalue the rupee against the dollar before the completion of its tenure in February, said a foreign fund manager on condition of anonymity.
THE NEWS
- A reduction of 1.3 billion rupees has been reported in November in customs duty collection as against September.
- The inflow of foreign investment in Pakistan has slowed down since the dismissal of prime minister Benazir Bhutto.
- The European Commission has committed food aid worth $11 million for Afghanistan.
- The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association urged the government to lift a ban on cellular telephones in Karachi and Hyderabad.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
